paper.title: Trust the Mass: Forced Weights in KV-Cache Eviction
paper.abstract: Every deployed sparse-attention or KV-cache-eviction rule keeps a subset of the keys, discards the rest, and renormalizes the attention weights over the kept set. Enumerating the exact best subset under that constraint on $168{,}192$ attention rows from five models shows that keeping the largest weights is already near-optimal, since the best subset closes only a median $2$ to $5\%$ of the remaining gap to full attention. If selection closes this little, published margins between eviction method

summary.core_problem: KV-cache eviction方法通常只保留一部分key/value，并把保留下来的attention权重重新归一化。该工作关注一个容易被忽略的问题：在这种“权重被原softmax强制固定”的算子里，子集选择本身还能带来多少收益，以及已有方法的性能差异到底来自选择质量、内存统计、query可见性，还是额外计算。
summary.importance: 对长上下文Serving和KV压缩研究的主要启发是：很多KV eviction方法的差异不能只看benchmark分数，必须同时核算真实占用字节、是否物理释放cache、是否使用query信息。论文给出的测量显示，保留最大attention mass的top-mass策略已经接近强制权重条件下的最优子集；因此，若两个方法都接近该子集上限，单靠更复杂的选择规则很难拉开大差距。这对设计预训练友好的长上下文模型也有参考意义，因为它提醒研究者区分“注意力近似误差”和“系统实现中的有效内存压缩”。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上，作者把单个attention row抽象为概率向量p和值向量v_j。dense attention输出为μ，保留集合A后输出为按原始权重在A上重新归一化得到的m_A。核心误差是es(A)=||μ-m_A||，对应实际KV eviction里的forced weights；作为对照，ef(A)允许在保留点上重新求权重，代表几何近似里的free weights。作者证明es(A)可由丢弃项的带权残差分解，并说明forced-weight最优子集ES(s)与free-weight最优子集EF(s)在数值和argmin上都可能不同。进一步，判定ES(s)=0在一维、均匀权重、整数点、s=N/2条件下仍是NP-complete，因此不应期待通用高效精确求解。实验上采用受限候选枚举来估计最优子集，同时提出一个从top-mass开始的greedy swap balancing selector作为便宜上界；该selector会读取dense输出μ，所以主要用于测量或decode-time分析，而不是无条件预压缩。
summary.experiments: 关键测量覆盖5个模型的168,192个attention rows。结果是，top-mass保留已经很接近forced-weight最优：最优子集相对top-mass只额外关闭了到dense attention剩余误差gap的中位数2%到5%。这说明选择规则的上限空间很小。作者随后在共享评测pipeline中审计已有KV eviction方法的实际内存使用，发现一些强的query-agnostic方法虽然名义上压缩cache，但由于per-head选择被存为mask，底层KV仍未物理缩小；只有ragged per-head storage才真正释放内存。在强制执行名义budget后，某些固定选择方法下降14.1到62.2个benchmark points；一个87.6点的retrieval差距被追溯到ranking时已经看到了question。作者提出的ContourKV是training-free的allocation rule，借用被比较方法自身的importance score，并在读结果前物理执行budget。它在160个与KVzip的比较中赢93次、输22次；在matched memory下与Compactor打平。这个打平结果反而支持核心结论：当selection接近forced-weight子集上限时，方法间难以凭选择质量继续拉开差距。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议约20到30分钟。优先看Introduction里对“selection quality、memory、query information、compute”的拆解；再看Operator and Frozen-Head Measurements中forced weights与free weights的形式化定义，以及top-mass接近最优的测量逻辑。若关心系统实现，重点看第4节的内存核算和budget enforcement实验。ContourKV本身可以快速扫过，重点不是新规则胜出，而是它作为受控对照验证了selection上限很低。附录A的NP-complete证明适合需要理论边界的读者细读。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a specific failure mode in KV-cache eviction: deployed operators keep a subset of keys, renormalize the original attention weights over that subset, and therefore operate under forced weights. The central question is how much subset selection can still improve the approximation under this constraint, and whether reported gaps between eviction methods actually come from selection quality, memory accounting, query visibility, or extra computation.
summary_en.importance: The useful lesson for long-context inference research is that KV eviction results need byte-level accounting. The paper shows that keeping the largest attention masses is already close to the best possible subset under forced weights. If this measurement holds, increasingly elaborate query-agnostic selectors have little headroom unless they change the operator, use query information, or exploit implementation details. This matters for pretraining-oriented long-context work as well, because model and data decisions should be separated from artifacts introduced by non-shrinking cache masks or unfair budget enforcement.
summary_en.technical_approach: The analysis models one attention row as a probability vector p over value vectors v_j. Dense attention returns μ, while a kept set A returns m_A, the original weights restricted to A and renormalized. The forced-weight error is es(A)=||μ-m_A||. This is contrasted with a free-weight geometric error ef(A), where weights on the retained points may be re-solved. The paper shows that these two objectives can differ in both value and minimizer. It also proves that deciding whether the forced-weight optimum ES(s) is zero is NP-complete even in a one-dimensional uniform-mass integer setting with s=N/2. Since the exact problem is combinatorial, the authors enumerate restricted candidates and use a cheap balancing selector that starts from the top-mass set and greedily swaps retained and dropped keys when the swap reduces es(A). This selector reads the dense output μ, so it is mainly a diagnostic and decode-time tool rather than a query-agnostic cache precompression rule.
summary_en.experiments: The main measurement enumerates exact best subsets on 168,192 attention rows from five models. The best subset improves over top-mass by only a median 2% to 5% of the remaining gap to full attention. The paper then audits established eviction methods in a shared evaluation pipeline. Several strong query-agnostic methods nominally compress the cache, but their per-head selections are stored as masks over a full non-shrinking cache; true memory savings require ragged per-head storage. Enforcing the nominal budget on fixed selections costs 14.1 to 62.2 benchmark points, and an 87.6-point retrieval gap is traced to rankings computed after the question is visible. The proposed ContourKV rule is training-free, reuses existing importance scores, and physically enforces the budget before evaluation. It wins 93 of 160 comparisons against KVzip and loses 22; at matched memory it ties Compactor, supporting the claim that near-optimal forced-weight selectors should not separate much by selection alone.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 20–30 minute skim is enough for most readers. Start with the Introduction for the decomposition of reported gains into selection, memory, query information, and compute. Then read the formal setup in Operator and Frozen-Head Measurements, especially the distinction between forced and free weights. Readers working on inference systems should focus on the memory-accounting experiments and budget enforcement results in Section 4. ContourKV is best read as a controlled probe rather than as the main contribution. Appendix A is useful if the computational hardness of the forced-weight subset problem matters for follow-up work.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会改变对 KV eviction 论文的信任基线；先看最优子集枚举和 bytes accounting，很多 margin 可能是评测假象。
recommendation.en: This should reset your trust baseline for KV-eviction papers; read the optimal-subset enumeration and byte accounting before believing reported margins.

paper.title: AutoVerifier: Residual-Guided Non-Parametric Optimization for Reference-Based Answer Verification
paper.abstract: Reference-based verifiers are important for evaluating reasoning models and providing accurate outcome rewards in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. To improve verification accuracy, prior work has explored rule-based, model-based, and tool-augmented verifiers for checking answer equivalence across diverse answer forms. However, the equivalence of answer forms such as $1+3.14$ and $1+π$ may depend on the question and scoring criterion. We frame such implicit assumptions as verifier

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文处理的是 reference-based answer verification 里的一个老问题：候选答案和参考答案是否等价，往往不只是字符串匹配或符号化简的问题，还隐含了题目语境、评分标准、数值容差、单位表达、近似形式是否可接受等“判题偏置”。现有 rule-based verifier 把逻辑写死，覆盖有限；model-based verifier 覆盖更广，但判定标准埋在模型行为里，不透明、不可编辑，也难以稳定复用。论文把这些隐含标准明确称为 verifier inductive biases，并试图从 verifier 的残差错误中自动归纳出来，再以可审计、可回放验证的形式沉淀为规则或 prompt 更新。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身不是核心论文，但对 post-train、RLVR、reward 建模和 benchmark 评测都很相关。原因很直接：只要训练依赖 outcome reward，verifier 的误判就会直接污染优化方向。很多 RL with verifiable rewards 工作默认 verifier 足够可靠，但实际难点常常不在算式能不能化简，而在“什么算对”这件事本身带有任务依赖的隐含标准。AutoVerifier 的价值在于，它没有再训练一个更大的 judge，而是把 verifier 改进做成一种非参数、可审计、可增量维护的过程。这对构建长期可维护的 reward pipeline 有现实意义，尤其适合数学、科学问答、结构化答案比对这类高频需要 verifier 的场景。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是 residual-guided non-parametric optimization。系统从一个固定 base verifier 出发，围绕它做迭代更新。每轮先在 construction pool 上回放当前 verifier，把预测与标注不一致的样本收集为 residuals。随后对这些 recurring errors 做模式归纳，形成 rule cards。每张 card 记录一种待补充的 verifier bias，包括支持样例、反例、适用条件，以及在什么情况下应 abstain。这里的设计很像把 verifier 的错误分析流程产品化：不是直接改模型参数，而是把 recurring mismatch 变成显式知识单元。

rule card 有两条晋升路径。若某种偏置可以写成确定性的比较逻辑，例如数值容差、单位归一化、科学计数法转换、某些符号等价规则，就进入 code audit 和 replay validation，通过后成为 code module。code module 是一个三值判定单元：Correct / Incorrect / Abstain。若某类偏置无法完全规则化，仍需要模型判断，则不写成代码，而是并入 fallback verifier 的 prompt guidance。最终推理时，系统先走模块库，能直接判的就直接输出，不能判的再交给固定的 model-based fallback。这个结构的关键优点有两个：一是把高频、稳定的比较逻辑前移为显式模块，降低对大模型 judge 的依赖；二是每次更新都要经过 replay validation，避免新规则修正局部错误的同时引入直接回归。

和已有方法相比，区别不在于又加了一个工具，而在于把 verifier 改进过程做成“残差发现—规则卡片—回放验证—模块/提示晋升”的闭环。它既不同于纯规则库的手工扩展，也不同于把所有复杂性都交给 judge model 吸收。
summary.experiments:
论文在四个 reference-based verification benchmark 上评测。主结果是 AutoVerifier 达到 93.05% macro accuracy，超过文中对比的 rule-based、model-based、scientific 和 tool-augmented verifier。更有信息量的是分组件结果：相对 prompt-only 设置，加入 code modules 后 macro accuracy 再提升 1.76 个点，说明收益不只是 prompt 改写，而是显式比较逻辑确实补上了 verifier 的盲区。与此同时，能够由模块直接完成的判定还把 fallback model 调用减少了 32.13%，这意味着不仅更准，也更省推理成本。

从论文描述看，实验重点不是追求某个 benchmark 上的极限分数，而是证明两件事：第一， recurring residuals 里确实存在可抽取、可复用的 verifier bias；第二，把这些 bias 以代码模块和 prompt guidance 分流实现，比单纯依赖 prompt 或单一 judge model 更稳。值得注意的是，这类结果的可信度很依赖 construction pool 与 benchmark 的分布关系；如果两者高度同分布，规则抽取会更容易。因此读实验时要特别看 replay validation、support/counterexample 设计，以及不同 benchmark 上的泛化是否一致。
summary.reading_guide:
泛读时先看 Introduction 里的几个例子，尤其是 1+3.14 与 1+π 在不同题目语境下是否等价的讨论。这个例子把论文要解决的问题讲得很清楚：不是形式化简能力不足，而是评分标准本身带条件。然后重点读 Method，抓住四个对象：residual、rule card、code module、fallback prompt。只要这四个对象之间的流转关系看明白，整篇方法就通了。

实验部分建议优先看总表和 ablation，尤其是 prompt-only vs +code modules，以及 fallback call reduction。预计 20 分钟左右可以完成泛读。若要进一步判断方法是否适合接入 RL reward pipeline，需要细看 replay validation 的通过标准、abstain 机制如何设计、以及错误模式聚类是否依赖较多人工参与。这些地方决定了它是一个可持续维护的 verifier 框架，还是一个需要较强人工运营的半自动系统。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a persistent issue in reference-based answer verification: answer equivalence is often governed not only by symbolic matching or numerical checking, but also by implicit grading assumptions tied to the question, acceptable approximation level, units, notation, and task context. Rule-based verifiers hard-code these assumptions and therefore have limited coverage. Model-based verifiers cover more cases, but the criteria remain buried inside model behavior, making them hard to audit, edit, and reuse. The paper frames these hidden criteria as verifier inductive biases and asks how to learn them from recurring verifier mistakes while keeping the resulting logic explicit and maintainable.
summary_en.importance: This is not a core pretraining paper, but it matters for post-training, RL with verifiable rewards, and evaluation infrastructure. Whenever outcome rewards depend on a verifier, verifier errors become optimization noise or, worse, systematic bias. Many RLVR pipelines assume the verifier is reliable enough, yet in practice the hard part is often not computation itself but deciding what should count as correct under a given scoring convention. AutoVerifier is useful because it improves the verifier without retraining a larger judge model. Instead, it turns verifier refinement into a non-parametric, auditable, incrementally maintainable process. That is practically relevant for math, science QA, and any structured-answer setting where reward quality depends on robust equivalence checking.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core method is residual-guided non-parametric optimization. The system starts from a fixed base verifier and iteratively improves it around observed mistakes. At each round, the current verifier is replayed on a construction pool, and disagreements with labels are collected as residuals. Recurring residual patterns are then abstracted into rule cards. Each card records a missing verifier bias together with support examples, counterexamples, applicability conditions, and abstention conditions. This is a key design choice: instead of directly updating model parameters, the method converts recurring failure modes into explicit knowledge units.

A rule card can follow one of two promotion paths. If the missing bias can be expressed as deterministic comparison logic—such as numerical tolerance handling, unit normalization, scientific notation conversion, or specific symbolic equivalence rules—it goes through code audit and replay validation, and if accepted becomes a code module. A code module is a deterministic verifier unit that returns Correct, Incorrect, or Abstain. If the bias cannot be fully codified and still requires model judgment, it is incorporated into the fallback verifier prompt rather than compiled into code. At inference time, the system first runs the module library; cases that can be decided explicitly are handled there, and only unresolved cases are sent to a fixed model-based fallback verifier.

What distinguishes this from prior work is not simply adding tools, but turning verifier improvement into a closed loop: residual discovery, rule-card drafting, replay validation, and promotion into either executable modules or prompt guidance. It sits between hand-maintained rule libraries and opaque judge-model behavior.
summary_en.experiments:
The paper evaluates on four reference-based verification benchmarks. The headline result is 93.05% macro accuracy, outperforming the reported rule-based, model-based, scientific, and tool-augmented baselines included in the study. The more informative result is the component ablation: compared with a prompt-only setting, adding code modules yields an additional +1.76 macro-accuracy gain. That suggests the benefit is not merely better prompting; explicit comparison logic is covering verifier blind spots that prompting alone does not fix. In addition, direct module decisions reduce fallback model calls by 32.13%, so the system improves both accuracy and inference efficiency.

The experiments are most convincing when read as evidence for two claims. First, recurring residuals do contain reusable verifier biases that can be extracted. Second, splitting those biases into deterministic modules versus prompt-level guidance works better than relying on a single prompt-only or model-only verifier. A careful reader should still pay attention to the relationship between the construction pool and the evaluation benchmarks: if they are too similar, rule extraction becomes easier. The replay-validation protocol, support/counterexample design, and cross-benchmark consistency are therefore important for judging how robust the method really is.
summary_en.reading_guide:
For a quick read, start with the motivating examples in the introduction, especially the discussion of when 1+3.14 should or should not be treated as equivalent to 1+π. That example captures the paper’s point well: the challenge is not only symbolic manipulation, but context-dependent grading assumptions. Then read the method section with four objects in mind: residuals, rule cards, code modules, and the fallback prompt. Once the transitions among these four are clear, the whole system becomes easy to follow.

In the experiments, prioritize the main comparison table and the ablations, especially prompt-only versus prompt-plus-code-modules, and the reduction in fallback calls. Around 20 minutes should be enough for a solid skim. If the goal is to assess whether this can plug into an RL reward pipeline, look more closely at replay-validation criteria, the abstain mechanism, and how much human effort is still needed to cluster or formalize recurring error patterns. Those details determine whether the method is a maintainable verifier framework or a semi-automatic workflow with significant manual overhead.

recommendation.zh: 如果你在做 RLVR 或 judge-based eval，这篇值得看；不是因为方法多新，而是它把 verifier bias 从黑盒误差变成可审计对象，先读 rule card 和 replay validation。
recommendation.en: Worth reading if you use RLVR or judge-based evaluation; the key idea is not novelty for its own sake, but turning verifier bias from opaque error into an auditable object—start with the rule-card and replay-validation parts.

paper.title: FrontierChallenge: Evaluating Scientific Workflow Completion
paper.abstract: Scientific agents increasingly analyze data, execute code, and produce research artifacts, yet most benchmarks emphasize final answers, isolated programs, or a single domain. We introduce FrontierChallenge, a cross-domain benchmark comprising 300 end-to-end scientific workflows. In this paper, we release and evaluate 97 of these tasks, spanning quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment. Each task provid

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是评测问题：现有科学 agent benchmark 往往只看最终答案、单段代码或单一学科任务，难以衡量模型是否能在固定目标和固定输入下，独立完成一个端到端、可复现、可验收的科学工作流。作者要测的不是“会不会做一点”，而是“能不能把整套流程交付完整”。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接关系不强，它更偏 agent evaluation。但它有两个启发点。第一，它把“部分进展”和“完整交付”明确分开，说明当前前沿模型即使在高平均分下，仍然缺少稳定完成长链条、多产物、多约束任务的能力。这对持续预训练、工具使用数据构造、以及 post-train 信号设计都有参考价值。第二，它提供了一个比单轮 QA 或单文件 coding 更接近真实科研执行的评测单元，能更好暴露模型在长程规划、状态管理、文件一致性、工具调用和错误恢复上的短板。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是构建 FrontierChallenge，一个跨六个科学领域的端到端工作流 benchmark。完整池子有 300 个任务，这次公开并评测其中 97 个，其余 203 个保留为内部 held-out。六个领域包括量子化学、分子动力学、材料表征、分析化学、生命科学、电化学/环境。

每个任务都被打包成自包含单元，至少包含五类元素：任务描述、固定输入、执行环境、交付物契约，以及 task-specific grader。作者强调四个设计原则：代表性、复杂性、多样性、可验证性。也就是说，任务必须像真实专业流程，必须是依赖多步分析和多种产物的完整流程，而不是把同一模板换参数；同时输出必须能通过文件、数值、图表或明确 acceptance criteria 自动评分。

评测指标上，主指标是 Pass Rate，即是否满足完整 task contract；Avg. Score 只作为辅助，表示部分完成度。这个设计很关键，因为很多 agent 在中间步骤上能做出不少东西，但最后交付包不一致、缺文件、数值不合格、图表与报告不匹配，实际并不能交付。作者还比较了 12 个前沿模型和 3 种 agent scaffold，并对 970 条 Claude Code 轨迹做了错误和最终状态分析，用来定位失败模式。
summary.experiments:
实验规模上，公开评测集是 97 个任务，模型数 12，agent scaffold 3 种。任务要求调用真实领域软件，例如 ORCA、CP2K、LAMMPS、AmberTools、PLUMED，并生成代码、分析结果、图表和报告等成套产物。

最关键的结果是“高部分分数、低完整通过率”的明显落差。表现最好的配置是 GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex 和 Grok 4.6 with Claude Code，完成 97 个任务中的 20 个，Pass Rate 只有 20.6%。但最高 Avg. Score 达到 87.9，说明模型经常能做对很多局部步骤，却无法满足完整交付契约。

这种落差在某些领域更明显。分析化学任务中，最高 Avg. Score 达到 87.6，但最高 Pass Rate 只有 4%；电化学/环境任务中，最高 Avg. Score 达到 94.9，但最高 Pass Rate 是 0%。这说明问题不只是知识缺失，而是长链条执行中的最后一公里：文件组织、结果一致性、格式要求、边界条件处理、以及多产物之间的相互约束。

作者还做了 failure analysis，统计 contract-breach signatures 和 Claude Code 轨迹中的 final-status / error behavior。虽然给出的正文片段没有展开全部细节，但从任务设计和指标定义可以看出，benchmark 更关注 agent 是否能在真实环境里把流程跑通，而不是在某个局部子任务上拿高分。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，不需要逐段精读。先看 Introduction，把 benchmark 的目标边界看清：它不是 autonomous science，也不是开放式科研发现，而是在目标、输入和环境固定后，测试 agent 是否能完成指定工作流。

然后重点看 FrontierChallenge 的任务构造原则和评测协议，尤其是 task package 的组成、Pass Rate 与 Avg. Score 的区别、以及为什么完整交付要作为主指标。这部分决定了 benchmark 的信息含量。

最后看结果表和 failure analysis，重点关注两个现象：一是不同 scaffold 对结果的影响，二是高 Avg. Score 却低 Pass Rate 的领域分布。预计 20-30 分钟可以完成一次有效泛读。

如果从基座研究角度带着问题去看，建议关注：哪些失败更像模型能力问题，哪些更像 post-train agent scaffold 问题；以及这类 benchmark 是否能反向指导 continual pretraining 或 tool-use 数据合成。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses an evaluation gap: most scientific-agent benchmarks measure final answers, isolated code snippets, or single-domain tasks, but do not test whether an agent can complete an end-to-end scientific workflow with fixed inputs, real tools, multiple dependent steps, and a verifiable bundle of deliverables. The target is not partial competence, but contract-level completion.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining-method paper, but it is still relevant as an evaluation asset for long-horizon agentic capability. Two points matter. First, it cleanly separates partial progress from full delivery, showing that frontier models can score highly on intermediate rubric items while still failing to produce a usable final artifact package. That has implications for continual pretraining, tool-use data generation, and post-training reward design. Second, it evaluates a more realistic unit of work than single-turn QA or single-file coding, exposing weaknesses in planning, state tracking, file consistency, tool execution, and recovery from intermediate errors.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core contribution is FrontierChallenge, a cross-domain benchmark of end-to-end scientific workflows. The full collection contains 300 tasks; 97 are released and evaluated in this work, while 203 remain held out internally. The released tasks span six domains: quantum chemistry, molecular dynamics, materials characterization, analytical chemistry, life science, and electrochemistry/environment.

Each task is packaged as a self-contained unit with aligned components including a task description, fixed inputs, an execution environment, a deliverable contract, and a task-specific grader. The curation follows four principles: representativeness, complexity, diversity, and verifiability. In practice, that means tasks must resemble real professional workflows, require dependency-aware multi-step execution, avoid trivial template variation, and support automated, repeatable scoring through files, numerical checks, plots, or explicit acceptance criteria.

The evaluation protocol is built around two metrics. Pass Rate is the primary metric and requires satisfying the full task contract. Avg. Score is secondary and measures partial progress under task-specific rubrics. This distinction is central to the paper: many agents can produce some correct intermediate outputs, but still fail the workflow because the final bundle is incomplete, inconsistent, or not reproducible. The authors evaluate 12 frontier models under 3 agent scaffolds and also analyze 970 Claude Code trajectories to characterize failure modes and end states.
summary_en.experiments:
The released benchmark contains 97 tasks, evaluated with 12 frontier models and 3 agent scaffolds. Tasks require real scientific software such as ORCA, CP2K, LAMMPS, AmberTools, and PLUMED, and demand executable code, quantitative analysis, visualizations, and evidence-grounded reports.

The main empirical result is a large gap between partial progress and full completion. The best-performing configurations—GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex and Grok 4.6 with Claude Code—complete only 20 of 97 tasks, corresponding to a Pass Rate of 20.6%. Yet the highest Avg. Score reaches 87.9. So the models often make substantial progress on substeps while still failing to satisfy the complete deliverable contract.

This gap is even sharper in some domains. In analytical chemistry, the highest Avg. Score is 87.6, but the best Pass Rate is only 4%. In electrochemistry/environment, the highest Avg. Score is 94.9, while the best Pass Rate is 0%. That pattern suggests the bottleneck is often not local scientific knowledge alone, but end-to-end execution reliability: file organization, consistency across outputs, formatting constraints, edge-case handling, and coherence among code, figures, tables, and prose.

The paper also includes failure analysis through contract-breach signatures and final-status/error behavior in 970 Claude Code trajectories. Even from the available text, the benchmark is clearly designed to stress workflow completion rather than isolated subskill performance.
summary_en.reading_guide:
This is a skim paper. Start with the introduction to understand the scope boundary: the benchmark is not about autonomous science or open-ended discovery, but about executing a specified workflow once the objective, inputs, and environment are fixed.

Then read the benchmark construction and evaluation protocol carefully, especially the task-package design, the distinction between Pass Rate and Avg. Score, and the rationale for using contract-level completion as the primary metric. That is where the benchmark gets its value.

Finally, inspect the main result tables and failure analysis. The two patterns worth tracking are the effect of different agent scaffolds and the domain-specific cases where Avg. Score is high but Pass Rate remains very low. A useful skim should take around 20-30 minutes.

From a foundation-model angle, the most useful questions are whether the observed failures are primarily model-capability failures or scaffold failures, and whether this benchmark can guide continual pretraining or tool-use data synthesis.

recommendation.zh: 一个极具挑战性的跨领域科学工作流 Benchmark，揭示了当前最强模型在长程、复杂科学任务上的严重不足（通过率仅20%），对评估模型的高级推理和规划能力很有价值。
recommendation.en: A highly challenging cross-domain scientific workflow benchmark revealing severe shortcomings of current top models in long-horizon, complex scientific tasks (only 20% pass rate). Valuable for evaluating advanced reasoning and planning capabilities.

paper.title: Where vs What: Decomposing Structural and Content Failures in LLM-Generated Structured Outputs
paper.abstract: Structured outputs such as JSON and tables are central to modern LLM-based systems, yet generation failures are evaluated monolithically, conflating two distinct error modes: placement errors (correct values at wrong positions) and value errors (wrong values at intended positions). We introduce Structure-Content Decomposition (SCD), a framework that independently measures structural fidelity and content accuracy. Applying SCD to nested JSON and table tasks across six models (7B to frontier), we

summary.core_problem: 现有的结构化输出（如 JSON、表格）评估方法将生成失败视为单一错误，无法区分“值错误”（生成了错误的内容）和“位置错误”（正确的内容放在了错误的结构位置）。
summary.importance: 提出了一种解耦结构与内容的评估框架，揭示了随着任务复杂度增加，LLM 的“结构保真度”比“内容准确度”退化得更早、更快的现象，并基于此设计了针对性的 RL 奖励机制，为提升 LLM 结构化输出能力提供了新视角。
summary.technical_approach: 引入结构-内容分解（SCD）框架，将评估分为三个层级：格式有效性、结构合规率（SCR）和值放置准确率（VPA）。通过对比“值存在率”（VP）和 VPA，量化“正确值放错位置”的比例。进一步，提出 SA-RLVR 方法，将 SCD 指标转化为 GRPO 的可验证奖励信号，直接优化模型的结构寻址能力。
summary.experiments: 在嵌套 JSON 和表格任务上评估了 6 个模型（7B 到前沿模型）。结果显示，在最高复杂度下，即使是 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 也会将 35% 的正确值放错位置，而 Qwen2.5-7B 的错放率高达 74%。消融实验表明这与模型依赖语义捷径有关。使用 SA-RLVR 训练后，JSON 值放置准确率从 0.26 提升至 0.63，显著优于 SFT 基线（0.28）。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读 SCD 框架的三个层级定义（图 2 和公式），理解如何通过 VP 和 VPA 的差值量化位置错误。关注实验部分关于“结构退化先于内容”的观察，以及 SA-RLVR 带来的显著性能提升。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing evaluations for structured outputs (e.g., JSON, tables) treat generation failures monolithically, failing to distinguish between 'value errors' (incorrect content) and 'placement errors' (correct content in the wrong structural position).
summary_en.importance: Introduces a decomposed evaluation framework that separates structure and content, revealing that structural fidelity degrades earlier and faster than content accuracy as complexity increases. It also provides a targeted RL reward mechanism based on these metrics, offering a new pathway to improve LLM structured generation.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes the Structure-Content Decomposition (SCD) framework, evaluating outputs hierarchically: format validity, Structural Compliance Rate (SCR), and Value Placement Accuracy (VPA). By comparing Value Presence (VP) with VPA, it quantifies the rate of misplaced correct values. Furthermore, it introduces SA-RLVR, which converts SCD metrics into verifiable rewards for GRPO to directly optimize structural addressing.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluated 6 models (7B to frontier) on nested JSON and table tasks. At the highest complexity, even DeepSeek-V4-Flash misplaced 35% of recalled values, while Qwen2.5-7B misplaced 74%. Ablations link this to reliance on semantic shortcuts. Training with SA-RLVR improved JSON VPA from 0.26 to 0.63, significantly outperforming a matched SFT baseline (0.28).
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on the definitions of the three SCD levels (Figure 2 and equations) to understand how placement errors are quantified via the gap between VP and VPA. Pay attention to the experimental observation of 'structure degrades first' and the substantial improvements achieved by SA-RLVR.

recommendation.zh: 只看 SCD 定义和复杂度曲线；它把“格式错”拆干净，可用于内部 tool-use/RLVR 数据诊断。
recommendation.en: Read the SCD definition and complexity curves; the clean split of format errors is useful for internal tool-use and RLVR diagnostics.

paper.title: Inter-dimension Dependence for Multi-Dimensional Evaluation of Open-Ended Text
paper.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge methods are widely used for evaluating the quality of generated open-ended text. Such evaluations are generally multi-dimensional, since the error patterns in texts can be different for different dimensions. Therefore, reliable LLM judges should evaluate each target dimension independently. To quantify the extent to which LLM judges depend on non-target dimensions when evaluating a target dimension, i.e., inter-dimension dependence, we propose CorrGap. To measure this, CorrGap use

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作处理的是一个常被忽略、但会直接影响 LLM-as-a-judge 可用性的问题：在多维文本评测里，模型是否真的在评“目标维度”，还是被其他非目标维度带偏。论文把这个现象定义为 inter-dimension dependence。比如评 relevance 时，judge 可能因为文本不流畅或不连贯而给低分，即便相关性本身并不差。这样一来，多维评测会退化成某种模糊的整体印象分，失去按维度诊断错误模式的意义。作者的核心目标有两个：先给出一个可量化的度量，判断这种维度串扰有多严重；再提出一个推理时干预方法，尽量让 judge 的打分依据只围绕目标维度展开。
summary.importance: 对预训练本身不是直接方法贡献，但对 post-train、reward design、LLM judge 可靠性有明确启发，尤其适合关心 RL/RLAIF 奖励信号质量的人。很多后训练流程默认多维 rubric 或多头奖励是“可分解”的，但这篇文章说明，若 judge 在维度间存在系统性耦合，那么看似细粒度的奖励其实可能仍是混杂信号。这个问题会传导到偏好学习、GRPO/PPO 奖励建模、合成监督数据筛选等环节。贡献量级更像“评测与诊断工具 + 一个推理时修正策略”，不是范式级方法，但问题定义是扎实的，且比单纯报 judge 准确率更接近真实使用场景。
summary.technical_approach:
技术上分两部分。第一部分是 CorrGap。它不是直接看某一维上的整体相关性，而是看：当一个样本在目标维度和其他维度上的真实分数差异很大时，judge 在该目标维度上的表现是否明显变差。作者先把每个维度的人工分数转成该维度内部的 percentile，避免不同维度原始分数分布不一致带来的偏差；然后对每个样本计算目标维度 percentile 与其他维度 percentile 均值的差值 Δ(t, d_i)。Δ 小的样本属于 low-variance group，说明目标维度和其他维度大致一致；Δ 大的样本属于 high-variance group，说明目标维度与其他维度明显背离。若 judge 能独立评估目标维度，那么它在两组上的相关性不应有系统差异；若存在维度串扰，则 high-variance 组更容易被非目标维度误导，导致相关性下降。CorrGap 就是两组相关性差值，并通过分层构造尽量控制目标维度真实分数分布，避免把“样本本来更难”误当成维度依赖。

第二部分是 DimCheck。它利用 judge 先生成的 CoT 作为可编辑中间表示。流程上，先让 judge 针对目标维度给出 reasoning；再用另一个检查步骤识别 reasoning 中哪些证据与目标维度无关，例如评 factuality 时引用了 fluency 或 style 的证据；然后迭代删除这些无关证据，并让模型基于清洗后的 CoT 重新打分。这个设计的关键不是重新训练 judge，而是在推理时约束其“证据使用范围”。论文还讨论了用较小模型去近似大模型的 DimCheck 组件，以降低额外推理成本。和直接改 prompt 相比，DimCheck 的区别在于它显式操作 reasoning 内容，而不是只靠一句“请只关注某维度”的指令。
summary.experiments: 实验覆盖四类开放式文本生成任务、三种评测框架、八个 judge 模型，以及三种用于验证和缓解的主力 LLM。全文主结论不是某个单点数字，而是现象具有普遍性：在多数任务、模型和框架组合下，CorrGap 都显著大于零，说明 inter-dimension dependence 不是个别 prompt 或个别模型的问题。作者还做了两类关键验证。第一类是度量有效性验证：在不同设置下，CorrGap 能稳定区分维度独立性更差的 judge，并且与人工观察到的 CoT 串扰现象一致。第二类是方法验证：DimCheck 相比强基线能更稳定地降低 CorrGap，并提升目标维度打分与人工标注的对齐。论文还展示了小模型蒸馏/逼近大模型检查器的结果，说明额外成本有压缩空间。由于给出的全文片段没有完整表格数字，无法可靠复述每个任务上的精确提升幅度，但从正文描述看，作者强调的是跨任务一致性和对强基线的稳定优势，而不是单一 benchmark 上的大幅提升。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读时建议抓三处。第一看 Introduction 和 CorrGap 定义部分，重点理解作者为什么不用整体相关性，而要比较 low-variance / high-variance 两组；这里决定了这个指标是否真的在测“维度串扰”而不是“样本难度”。第二看方法细节里 percentile 归一化和分组控制的设计，这部分是在补统计口径上的漏洞，值得确认是否足够严谨。第三看 DimCheck 的案例和消融，尤其是“删除无关证据后为何能改善打分”以及“小模型近似大模型检查器”的成本收益。预计 20–30 分钟可以完成有效泛读；如果你做 reward model、judge 或 rubric-based RL，建议把实验设置和附录 prompt 也一起看。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a failure mode in multi-dimensional LLM judging: when a judge is asked to score one target dimension, its decision may still be influenced by other non-target dimensions. In practice, this means a relevance score can be dragged down by poor fluency, or a factuality score can be inflated by overall coherence. Once this happens, multi-dimensional evaluation collapses toward a vague overall impression score, which defeats the purpose of dimension-wise diagnosis. The paper therefore asks two concrete questions: how to measure this inter-dimension dependence reliably, and how to reduce it at inference time without retraining the judge.
summary_en.importance: This is not a pretraining-method paper, but it matters for post-training pipelines that rely on LLM judges, especially RL with rubric-style rewards, synthetic supervision filtering, and reward modeling for open-ended tasks. A key implication is that decomposed rewards are not automatically disentangled. If the judge internally mixes dimensions, the training signal remains entangled even when the interface looks fine-grained. That makes the work relevant to anyone concerned with reward quality, reward hacking, and the reliability of LLM-based evaluators. The contribution is best viewed as a diagnostic metric plus a mitigation procedure, rather than a new alignment paradigm.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The paper has two main components. First is CorrGap, a metric for inter-dimension dependence. Instead of measuring only the overall correlation between judge scores and human scores on a target dimension, CorrGap asks whether the judge becomes less accurate exactly on examples where the target dimension differs strongly from the other dimensions. The authors convert human scores within each dimension into percentiles, which avoids artifacts from different score distributions across dimensions. For each text and target dimension, they compute the gap between the target-dimension percentile and the mean percentile of the non-target dimensions. Small-gap examples form a low-variance group; large-gap examples form a high-variance group. If the judge evaluates the target dimension independently, its correlation with human labels should be similar across the two groups. If it leaks information from non-target dimensions, the high-variance group should suffer more, because those are precisely the cases where dimensions disagree. CorrGap is defined from this correlation difference, with additional care to control for target-score distribution so that the metric does not simply reflect example difficulty.

The second component is DimCheck, an inference-time intervention over chain-of-thought. The judge first produces reasoning for the target dimension. A checking step then identifies evidence in that reasoning that is unrelated to the target dimension, such as comments about fluency when scoring factuality. Those irrelevant pieces are iteratively removed, and the model re-evaluates the text conditioned on the cleaned reasoning. The key idea is to constrain the evidence basis of the score, rather than only changing the instruction prompt. The paper also explores using smaller models to approximate the larger-model checking component, which is important because the method otherwise adds nontrivial inference overhead.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments span four open-ended generation tasks, three evaluation frameworks, eight judge models for the diagnostic study, and three main LLMs for the mitigation study. The central empirical result is broad rather than benchmark-specific: CorrGap is consistently positive in most settings, indicating that inter-dimension dependence is pervasive rather than anecdotal. The paper also validates CorrGap itself by showing that it aligns with observed chain-of-thought contamination patterns and can distinguish judges with worse dimension independence. For mitigation, DimCheck reduces CorrGap and improves alignment with human scores compared with strong baselines. Another practical result is that a smaller model can approximate the larger DimCheck component with lower inference cost. The full tables are not available in the provided excerpt, so it would be unsafe to invent exact gains, but the paper’s emphasis is on consistency across tasks and frameworks rather than one unusually large number.
summary_en.reading_guide: For a quick read, focus on three parts. First, read the problem framing and the CorrGap definition carefully; the main value of the paper depends on whether the metric isolates dimension leakage rather than generic difficulty. Second, inspect the percentile normalization and grouping strategy, since that is where most statistical confounds would enter. Third, read the DimCheck examples and ablations to see whether removing irrelevant reasoning actually changes the evidence basis of the score in a meaningful way. A useful reading path is Introduction, metric definition, method overview, then experiments and appendix prompts. Around 20 to 30 minutes is enough for a solid skim; spend longer if you work on reward models, LLM judges, or rubric-based RL.

recommendation.zh: 做 RLHF 或 judge-based eval 的人该看；不是范式突破，但把“多维打分其实在偷看别的维度”这件事量化了，先读 CorrGap 定义和消融。
recommendation.en: Worth reading if you rely on LLM judges for RLHF or eval; not a paradigm shift, but it cleanly quantifies cross-dimension leakage—start with the CorrGap definition and ablations.

paper.title: BenchBench-Protocol: Evaluating Real-World Wet-Lab Protocol Reasoning and Modification
paper.abstract: We introduce BenchBench-Protocol, a benchmark for large language models of 149 protocol-modification tasks recovered from modifications that scientists made to published protocols during real experimental work. Adapting a published protocol to a new experiment is a routine task for a wet-lab scientist, and a correct modification requires accounting for prior choices and downstream steps. Recent life-science benchmarks have moved toward open-ended, rubric-graded tasks, but tasks are typically eli

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是一个评测问题：现有生命科学 LLM benchmark 虽然越来越开放式，但很多任务是专家“设计出来”的，不一定贴近真实实验室里科学家如何修改 protocol。BenchBench-Protocol 试图用真实工作流中发生过的 protocol 修改记录，构造一个更接近实际科研决策分布的 benchmark，考察模型是否能根据已有 protocol、实验目标和下游依赖，提出合理修改方案。
summary.importance: 对基座预训练研究的直接价值较弱。它不是训练方法、数据配比、优化或建模范式论文，而是一个垂直领域 benchmark。保留它的唯一理由，是它在评测构造上有一点方法论意义：任务不是凭空写，而是从真实版本差异中恢复；rubric 也绑定了具体修改及其 downstream consequences。这种“从真实工作流痕迹反推任务”的做法，对通用 agent 或科研助手评测有参考价值。但如果只从 LLM pretrain 研究视角看，它更接近领域应用评测，不属于优先阅读对象。
summary.technical_approach: 数据构造流程是全文最重要的部分。作者从 Benchling 上科学家修改过的 protocol 版本出发，将其与公开发表的原始 protocol 对比，提取差异；这些差异被转写成第一人称、自然语言风格的 scientist query，同时生成带权重的 rubric，要求回答不仅指出该改什么，还要覆盖相关的下游影响。任务覆盖九个湿实验生物学领域，共 149 个任务，来自 96 个已发表 protocol。每个任务至少经过两位相关领域 PhD 且有三年以上实验经验的科学家独立审阅，审查维度包括问题相关性、科学正确性、rubric 推理深度、rubric 科学准确性和整体质量，只有高评分样本被保留。评测时，模型可使用互联网搜索工具，输出自由文本答案；评分采用 LLM-as-a-judge，对 rubric 中每个 criterion 单独打 0/1/2 分，再按权重汇总成归一化分数。作者还做了 grader 一致性检查，并限制评分尺度较粗，以提高 judge 稳定性。
summary.experiments: 实验评估了 9 个模型，包括 Claude Opus 5、GPT-5.6 系列、Gemini 3.6 Flash、Grok 4.5、Kimi K3、GLM 5.2 和 Inkling。每个任务采样 10 次，若回答格式错误或拒答则记 0 分，并单独统计 invalid-response rate。模型输入包括 query、原始 protocol 和互联网访问权限；闭源模型使用各自原生搜索工具，开源模型通过 Exa 搜索。结果汇总为 0 到 1 的 normalized rubric score。就全文可见内容看，作者更强调 benchmark 构造质量和评分协议，而不是某个模型显著领先多少；关键实验信息在于：1）任务是真实 protocol 修改恢复而来，而非专家虚构；2）rubric 是加权、逐项评分，减少开放式回答评测的随意性；3）做了 grader model 间一致性验证。若关心具体模型排名和不同 intent/domain 的分项表现，需要看表格和附录，因为当前提供的正文片段没有完整数值。
summary.reading_guide: 如果只是判断是否值得读，先看 Introduction 和 Benchmark Design。重点不是模型结果，而是任务来源是否真实、rubric 是否可操作、审稿流程是否足够严。再看 Experimental Setup，确认 tool-use 配置、judge 方案和多次采样协议。预计 10–15 分钟可以完成一次泛读。若只从基座研究角度出发，可以把它当作一个“真实工作流评测构造案例”来看，不必深读全部生物学任务细节。真正值得留意的是任务恢复方式和 weighted rubric 设计，而不是生命科学本身。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses an evaluation problem rather than a modeling one. Many recent life-science LLM benchmarks are open-ended, but the tasks are often written by experts from scratch and may not reflect how scientists actually modify protocols during real lab work. BenchBench-Protocol tries to recover tasks from real protocol edits, so the benchmark measures whether a model can adapt an existing protocol while accounting for prior choices and downstream experimental consequences.
summary_en.importance: Its direct relevance to foundation-model pretraining is limited. This is not a paper about training objectives, data mixture, optimization, scaling, or model architecture. It is a domain-specific benchmark. The part that may still interest LLM researchers is the benchmark-construction methodology: tasks are reconstructed from real workflow traces rather than invented, and the rubric is tied to concrete modifications and their downstream dependencies. That design could be useful for future agent or scientific-assistant evaluation. Still, from a pretraining-centered perspective, this is not a priority read.
summary_en.technical_approach: The main contribution is the dataset and evaluation protocol. The authors start from protocol versions modified by scientists on Benchling and compare them against published source protocols. The observed differences are converted into first-person scientist queries and weighted rubrics. A correct answer is expected not only to propose the modification itself, but also to address downstream implications. The benchmark contains 149 tasks derived from 96 published protocols across nine wet-lab biology domains. Each task is reviewed by at least two independent scientists with a relevant PhD and at least three years of bench experience. Review criteria include question relevance, scientific soundness, rubric reasoning depth, rubric scientific accuracy, and overall quality; only high-quality tasks are retained. During evaluation, models receive the query, the source protocol, and internet access, and produce a free-form answer. Scoring is done with an LLM judge that evaluates each rubric criterion separately on a 0/1/2 scale, then aggregates with criterion weights into a normalized score. The paper also reports grader-consistency checks and intentionally uses a coarse scoring scale to improve judge stability.
summary_en.experiments: Nine models are evaluated, including Claude Opus 5, the GPT-5.6 family, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5, Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, and Inkling. Each task is attempted ten times. Invalid outputs, such as formatting failures or refusals, are assigned zero and tracked separately. Models are given the query, the published protocol, and web access; proprietary models use their native search tools, while open models use Exa. Performance is reported as a normalized weighted-rubric score between 0 and 1. From the available text, the paper emphasizes benchmark quality and evaluation protocol more than headline model gaps. The key empirical points are: (1) tasks come from real protocol modifications rather than synthetic expert-authored prompts, (2) scoring is criterion-wise and weighted, which makes open-ended evaluation more structured, and (3) grader agreement was checked across representative judge models. For exact model rankings and breakdowns by intent or biology domain, the tables and appendices would need to be consulted, since the provided text does not include the full numeric results.
summary_en.reading_guide: If the goal is triage, read the Introduction and Benchmark Design first. The important question is not which model wins, but whether the task source is genuinely realistic, whether the rubric is operational, and whether expert review is strong enough. Then read the Experimental Setup to understand tool-use conditions, the judge protocol, and the repeated-sampling design. A useful skim should take about 10–15 minutes. From a foundation-model perspective, it is best treated as a case study in realistic workflow-grounded benchmark construction rather than as a biology paper to study in depth. The most transferable ideas are the task-recovery pipeline and the weighted rubric design.

recommendation.zh: 看它的“diff→加权 rubric”构造法：比专家拍脑袋出题更干净；但领域偏湿实验，先确认你的 eval 需求再投入复现。
recommendation.en: Focus on the diff-to-weighted-rubric construction—it’s cleaner than expert-elicited prompts; domain is wet-lab heavy, so validate fit before investing in reproduction.

paper.title: OmniJudge or OmniBias? Diagnosing Multimodal Judges through Balanced, Decoupled Lenses
paper.abstract: Multimodal understanding models that can jointly judge text-to-image (T2I), text-to-video (T2V) and text-to-speech (TTS) generation are increasingly used as "OmniJudges" for evaluation and automatic annotation. How reliably they understand what they score remains unclear, since existing benchmarks and training data tend to overemphasize positive examples and to conflate distinct failure modes, so a judge may score well without recognizing failures while its capability gaps stay hidden. Motivated

summary.core_problem: 现有多模态 judge / reward model 评测容易高估模型能力。原因是样本分布偏向正例和高质量输出，且多个失败模式常被混在一个总分里。模型即使不会识别细粒度错误，也可能靠数据先验拿到不错分数。D3-Omni 要诊断的是：OmniJudge 在 T2I、T2V、TTS 三类生成结果上，是否真正理解它正在打分的维度。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的直接价值在于评测信号质量。多模态 judge 正在被用于自动标注、偏好数据构造、reward model 训练和蒸馏教师。如果 judge 对中等质量样本、罕见错误或特定模态存在系统偏差，后续 SFT/RL 数据会把这些偏差放大。D3-Omni 的贡献不是提出更强模型，而是把 judge 评测从粗粒度偏好准确率推进到平衡、可归因的诊断评测。它对构造多模态 post-train 数据和 reward 数据尤其有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: 方法核心是平衡和解耦。D3-Omni 覆盖 T2I、T2V、TTS 三个任务，共 53 个正交二分类维度，分别为 17、22、14 个维度；样本总数 10,671，三类任务分别为 3,526、1,998、5,147。每个维度尽量控制正负样本比例，同时覆盖不同总质量区间，避免模型通过“多数样本是好样本”这一先验获得虚高准确率。它没有简单重新生成一批媒体样本，而是围绕已有生成结果进行维度化构造、模型辅助过滤、一致性检查和人工核验，把人工成本集中在质量控制上。评测时不只看总分，还看各分数区间的 segment accuracy，以及预测总分相对期望分数的偏差，用来区分 Yes-bias 和 No-bias。
summary.experiments: 实验主要评估多个闭源和开源 omni / multimodal judge。图 1 给出几个稳定现象。第一，T2I、T2V、TTS 上的分段准确率都呈 U 形：低分和高分样本相对容易，中间质量区间明显变难。这说明 judge 对“局部正确但有细节错误”的样本识别不足。第二，TTS 最弱，最高配置 Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus 的整体 segment accuracy 为 65.7%，Gemini-3.1-Pro 为 60.7%，Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash 为 60.4%，Gemini-3-Flash 为 60.2%。T2I 和 T2V 表现较高，但仍不稳：T2I 中 Gemini-3.1-Pro 为 78.6%，Gemini-3.5-Flash 为 77.6%，Gemini-3-Flash 为 77.5%；T2V 中 Gemini-3.5-Flash 为 76.7%，Gemini-3.1-Pro 为 76.0%，Gemini-3-Flash 为 75.2%。第三，总分偏差曲线显示不同模型存在系统性 Yes-bias 或 No-bias，且偏差随期望分数区间变化，不是一个简单可校准的常数偏移。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 20–30 分钟。重点看 introduction 中关于为什么 judge benchmark 需要分布平衡的论证，以及 benchmark construction 部分对“balanced”和“decoupled”的具体定义。图 1 是最关键结果，能快速看到中间分数区间退化和模态差异。若关心多模态 reward data，可以再看维度 taxonomy、样本构造流程和偏差度量方式。对基座预训练本身没有训练 recipe 层面的新方法，但对评估自动标注器和 reward model 的可靠性有实际参考。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing evaluations of multimodal judge and reward models can overestimate judging ability. The main issue is distributional bias: datasets are often dominated by positive or high-quality samples, while different failure modes are collapsed into a single score. A model can look accurate without detecting fine-grained errors. D3-Omni asks whether omni-modal judges actually understand the T2I, T2V, and TTS outputs they score.
summary_en.importance: The work matters for the quality of training signals. Multimodal judges are increasingly used for automatic annotation, preference labeling, reward modeling, and distillation. If these judges miss mid-quality failures or show modality-specific bias, SFT and RL pipelines can inherit and amplify those errors. The contribution is an evaluation asset rather than a new model: it turns judge evaluation into a balanced, diagnosable, dimension-level measurement problem.
summary_en.technical_approach: D3-Omni is built around balance and decoupling. It covers T2I, T2V, and TTS with 53 orthogonal binary dimensions, split into 17, 22, and 14 dimensions. The benchmark contains 10,671 samples: 3,526 for T2I, 1,998 for T2V, and 5,147 for TTS. Each dimension is designed to maintain positive-negative parity and to cover different score intervals, so that a judge cannot rely on the prior that most generations are acceptable. Instead of regenerating all outputs, the construction process uses dimension-oriented sample assembly, model-assisted filtering, consistency checks, and targeted human verification. Evaluation reports segment accuracy across score ranges and total-score deviation, which exposes Yes-bias and No-bias rather than hiding them behind one aggregate number.
summary_en.experiments: The experiments evaluate a range of closed and open omni-modal judges. Figure 1 shows three useful patterns. First, segment accuracy follows a U shape in T2I, T2V, and TTS: very low- and high-quality samples are easier, while mid-score samples are much harder. This is exactly the regime where local errors are embedded in otherwise plausible outputs. Second, TTS remains the weakest modality. The best reported TTS segment accuracy is 65.7% for Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus, followed by Gemini-3.1-Pro at 60.7%, Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash at 60.4%, and Gemini-3-Flash at 60.2%. T2I and T2V are higher but still imperfect: Gemini-3.1-Pro reaches 78.6% on T2I, while Gemini-3.5-Flash reaches 76.7% on T2V. Third, total-score deviation plots reveal systematic Yes-bias or No-bias, and the bias changes across score intervals rather than behaving like a constant calibration error.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 20–30 minutes. The most useful parts are the motivation for balanced judge benchmarks, the exact definition of balanced and decoupled dimensions, and Figure 1. Readers working on multimodal reward data should also inspect the dimension taxonomy, sample construction pipeline, and score-deviation metrics. The work does not provide a new pretraining recipe, but it is useful for auditing the reliability of automatic annotators and reward models.

recommendation.zh: 做多模态自动标注或 judge 训练的人可以看；它不改预训练范式，但 benchmark 设计很干净，适合拿来检查你家的 reward/judge 是否只学会了偏置。
recommendation.en: Worth a skim if you train multimodal judges or use them for auto-labeling; it will not change pretraining priors, but the benchmark design is clean and useful for exposing shortcut-heavy reward models.

paper.title: SA-Bench: Evaluating Semantic Alignment in LLM-Based Paper Reproduction
paper.abstract: LLM agents can generate paper reproduction code, yet often produce scientifically unfaithful implementations. We define this failure mode as semantic drift, where generated code silently diverges from the paper's specifications. We introduce SemanticAlign-Bench(SA-Bench), a diagnostic benchmark covering 30 papers from ICLR, ICML and NeurIPS 2025. For each paper, we decompose its specifications into atomic and verifiable implementation claims, which we call Semantic Alignment Units (SAUs) and eva

summary.core_problem: LLM coding agent 在复现机器学习论文时，常能生成可运行代码，却没有忠实实现论文规格。SA-Bench 把这种问题定义为 semantic drift，即代码在数值、方法、实验协议或执行顺序上悄悄偏离论文描述。
summary.importance: 这项工作对基座研究的价值在于评估长上下文代码 agent 的真实任务理解能力。论文复现不是普通代码补全，模型需要从正文、公式、表格、附录中抽取分散规格，并把它们转成一致的工程实现。这个能力与长文档理解、代码生成、科学推理和 agent scaffold 的设计都有关系。SA-Bench 的启发是：只看代码能否运行或结果是否接近，不能定位科学实现是否忠实；需要把论文规格拆成可验证的原子实现声明，再逐条检查。
summary.technical_approach: SA-Bench 将 paper-to-code 复现评测形式化为静态的 claim-level scoring。输入是一篇论文 P 和一个生成的代码仓库 R，输出是论文级 Semantic Alignment Score 以及每个 claim 的诊断判断。核心单元是 Semantic Alignment Unit，简称 SAU。每个 SAU 必须满足三点：能定位到论文中的具体来源片段；能通过静态代码检查验证；只描述一个独立实现决策。漂移类型分为四类：D1 Numerical Precision，关注超参数、阈值、结构维度；D2 Method / Formula，关注算法步骤、公式和组件接口；D3 Protocol，关注数据处理、训练设置和实验规范；D4 Ordering，关注操作执行顺序。评分不执行代码，而是使用面向不同维度的 LLM judge，按五级 rubric 给出判断。这种设计牺牲了端到端行为验证，但减少了随机种子、环境、算力和数据处理差异带来的混淆。
summary.experiments: 基准包含 30 篇来自 ICLR、ICML、NeurIPS 2025 的论文，覆盖五个机器学习领域和六类研究范式。标注得到 1,491 个经过人工核验的 SAU。实验评估 12 种生成配置，即 4 个模型乘以 3 个 scaffold，共 360 个 paper-level evaluation。主要结论是 semantic drift 在所有配置中都系统存在；面向 executability 优化的 scaffold 对科学复现忠实度帮助有限。换言之，让仓库能跑起来并不等价于实现了论文声称的方法。给出的分类结果还显示，不同漂移类型需要分开看，否则单一总分会掩盖是超参数误读、公式实现错误，还是实验协议偏离。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，约 25–35 分钟。重点看第 3 节对 SAU 的定义、四类 drift taxonomy，以及 extraction / judging pipeline。Table 1 有助于理解它与 PaperBench、SciCoQA 等工作的差异。若做 coding agent 或 paper-to-code 系统，建议细看 Appendix B.1 的 SAU 标注 schema 和 Appendix C 的 taxonomy 来源。对预训练研究员来说，最有用的是它把“长文档规格理解”拆成可监督、可诊断原子单元的方法，而不是最终 leaderboard 数字。

summary_en.core_problem: LLM coding agents can produce executable repositories for paper reproduction, but the code often fails to implement the paper faithfully. SA-Bench names this failure mode semantic drift: silent divergence from the paper specification in numerical values, method logic, experimental protocol, or execution order.
summary_en.importance: The benchmark is useful for studying long-context code agents and scientific task understanding. Paper reproduction requires a model to gather scattered specifications from methods, equations, tables, and appendices, then translate them into a coherent implementation. This is closer to specification grounding than ordinary code generation. The key lesson is that executability and aggregate reproduction results are not enough; scientific fidelity needs claim-level verification against the source paper.
summary_en.technical_approach: SA-Bench formulates paper-to-code evaluation as static claim-level scoring. Given a paper P and a generated repository R, the system outputs a paper-level Semantic Alignment Score and per-claim diagnostic judgments. The basic unit is the Semantic Alignment Unit, or SAU. An SAU must be localizable to a source span in the paper, verifiable by static code inspection, and atomic enough to represent one independent implementation decision. The taxonomy covers four drift types: D1 Numerical Precision for hyperparameters, thresholds, and architectural dimensions; D2 Method / Formula for algorithmic steps, equations, and component interfaces; D3 Protocol for data processing, training setup, and experimental rules; and D4 Ordering for procedural sequence. The evaluation uses dimension-specific LLM judges with a five-level rubric, without executing the repository. This avoids confounding from seeds, environments, compute budgets, and dataset variations, although it cannot replace behavioral testing.
summary_en.experiments: The benchmark contains 30 papers from ICLR, ICML, and NeurIPS 2025, spanning five ML domains and six research paradigms. It includes 1,491 human-verified SAU claims. The evaluation covers 12 generator configurations, formed by 4 models and 3 scaffolds, for 360 paper-level evaluations. The reported finding is that semantic drift appears systematically across all configurations. Scaffolds optimized for executability provide limited improvement in scientific fidelity. In practice, a repository that runs can still miss the claimed algorithm, use the wrong numerical setting, or follow a different protocol. The four-way taxonomy is therefore important because a single score would hide the type of failure.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 25–35 minutes. Focus on Section 3 for the SAU definition, the drift taxonomy, and the extraction and judging pipeline. Table 1 is useful for comparing the benchmark with PaperBench and related paper-to-code evaluations. For coding-agent researchers, Appendix B.1 on the annotation schema and Appendix C on the taxonomy construction are the most actionable parts. For pretraining researchers, the main value is the decomposition of long-document specification understanding into verifiable atomic units.

recommendation.zh: 把“复现”从跑通提升到“规格对齐”是对的；直接看 SAU 的定义与四类 drift 统计，能校准你对 coding agent 评测的预期。
recommendation.en: Good move: reproduction should be spec-alignment, not just runnable code; read the SAU formulation and drift breakdown to recalibrate coding-agent evaluation.

paper.title: TRACE: An Evidence-Grounded Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of Large Reasoning Models
paper.abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) generate intermediate reasoning traces that may contain unsafe content, even when their final responses appear safe. Guardrail models are designed to detect and block unsafe content, yet existing benchmarks for unsafe content detection focus primarily on prompts and final responses, leaving reasoning traces largely unexamined. Moreover, these benchmarks typically provide only binary safety labels, without evidence annotations that justify the judgments. To address t

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作关注大型推理模型的安全评测盲点：中间 reasoning trace 可能包含不安全内容，但现有 guardrail benchmark 大多只看输入 prompt 和最终回答，忽略了推理过程本身。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是 safety benchmark。它把安全评测从 prompt/final-response 扩展到完整推理链路，并加入 evidence-grounded 标注。对基座预训练的直接作用有限，但对 reasoning model 的 post-train 与 guardrail 评测有现实价值。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 TRACE，一个覆盖 prompt、reasoning trace、final response 三层的安全评测基准。数据包含双语 prompt、9 类风险、10 种攻击策略；对每个 prompt，使用 4 个大型推理模型生成 reasoning trace 和最终回答，并对各组件做安全标注，同时抽取支持证据，避免只有二元标签而缺少可审计依据。
summary.experiments: 摘要称评测了 18 个 guardrail 模型，但未给出具体模型名称、数据总量和关键数值。实验重点应是比较 guardrail 在不同输入层级上的检测能力，尤其检验它们对 reasoning trace 的覆盖是否显著弱于对 prompt 或 final response 的检测。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper targets a blind spot in safety evaluation for large reasoning models: intermediate reasoning traces can contain unsafe content even when the final answer looks safe, yet most guardrail benchmarks only evaluate prompts and final responses.
summary_en.importance: This is a safety benchmark contribution. It extends evaluation from prompt/final-response pairs to the full reasoning pipeline and adds evidence-grounded annotations. The direct relevance to pretraining is limited, but it matters for post-training and guardrail evaluation of reasoning models.
summary_en.technical_approach: The work introduces TRACE, a benchmark covering prompts, reasoning traces, and final responses. It includes bilingual prompts, nine risk categories, and ten attack strategies. For each prompt, four large reasoning models generate traces and final answers, and each component is annotated for safety with supporting evidence, rather than only binary labels.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports evaluation of 18 guardrail models, but does not provide dataset size, model names, or headline numbers. The key empirical question is whether guardrails are substantially weaker on reasoning traces than on prompts or final responses.

recommendation.zh: 做 reasoning model 安全或 verifier 的人可以留档；对预训练帮助不大，但它提醒一个现实问题：只盯 final answer 的安全评测会系统性漏检中间链路。
recommendation.en: Keep it on file if you work on reasoning-model safety or verifiers; not very relevant to pretraining, but it usefully highlights that final-answer-only safety evaluation systematically misses unsafe intermediate traces.

paper.title: PeakBench: Benchmarking Resource-Aware Tool Invocation in LLM Agents
paper.abstract: LLM agents increasingly solve tasks by invoking multiple tools, where parallel execution is essential for low latency but difficult to manage safely. Existing agent benchmarks primarily evaluate tool selection, argument generation, and end-to-end success under mostly serial execution, largely overlooking valid parallelization and resource-constrained scheduling. This missing scheduling dimension creates a practical failure mode: serial execution is safe but slow, while resource-agnostic parallel

summary.core_problem: 现有 LLM agent benchmark 主要评估工具选择和最终成功率，但基本忽略了并行调用中的资源约束与调度正确性，导致无法衡量“安全但慢”和“快但会爆资源”之间的真实能力差异。
summary.importance: 这是一个评测贡献。它补上了 agent tool-use 里很实际但常被漏掉的一维：资源感知的并行调度。对做通用 agent 系统、tool planner、execution policy 的研究有参考价值，但对基座预训练本身的直接牵引较弱。
summary.technical_approach: 论文提出 PeakBench：由可执行的多工具工作流组成，带有基于执行的依赖标注和实测资源画像。核心设计是两段式评估，把失败归因拆成依赖规划错误与资源约束调度错误，避免只看端到端成功率而掩盖具体短板。
summary.experiments: 从摘要可知，实验重点不是更大模型或训练，而是 benchmark 构建与评测协议验证。主要比较对象应是现有 agent 在串行执行、资源无感并行执行以及资源约束调度下的表现差异；摘要未给出具体模型规模、样本量和数值结果。

summary_en.core_problem: Existing LLM-agent benchmarks mostly test tool selection and end-task success, but largely miss the scheduling dimension of parallel tool execution under resource constraints.
summary_en.importance: This is primarily an evaluation contribution. It adds a practically important axis—resource-aware parallel scheduling—to tool-use benchmarks. Useful for agent-system research, but only indirectly relevant to foundation-model pretraining.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper introduces PeakBench, a benchmark of executable multi-tool workflows with execution-grounded dependency annotations and measured resource profiles. Its key design is a two-part evaluation framework that disentangles dependency-planning errors from resource-constrained scheduling errors.
summary_en.experiments: From the abstract, the emphasis is on benchmark construction and protocol validation rather than model scaling or training. The likely comparisons are serial execution, resource-agnostic parallelism, and resource-aware scheduling, though the abstract does not provide model sizes or full quantitative tables.

recommendation.zh: 和 pretrain 关系不深，但如果你在看 tool-use agent 的真实瓶颈，只读任务定义和 failure attribution 设计就够了，别把它当能力提升论文。
recommendation.en: Not very pretrain-relevant, but if you care about real tool-use bottlenecks, read the task design and failure attribution only; this is an eval paper, not a capability advance.

paper.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
paper.abstract: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly used as learned simulators for policy evaluation and improvement, yet their effectiveness rests on an unverified assumption: generated futures faithfully reflect arbitrary valid actions. Existing benchmarks are typically confined to expert demonstrations, leaving off-expert action following inadequately evaluated. To address this gap, we introduce WorldEcho, which probes action following over a broader action distribution using visual integrity an

summary.core_problem: 检验机器人动作条件世界模型是否真的按照给定动作生成未来状态，尤其是在非专家动作分布上是否失效。
summary.importance: 贡献是对 action-conditioned world model 的诊断与校准方法，问题接近具身多模态生成和策略学习中的模型可靠性；对 LLM 预训练不是直接方法，但对“生成模型是否服从条件信号”的评测有参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 提出 WorldEcho，用视觉完整性和 SE(3) 轨迹对齐评估动作跟随能力；进一步提出 WorldSync，从动作后果分布覆盖、表征 grounding、干预效应对齐三个方向增强模型对动作条件的响应。
summary.experiments: 摘要显示，现有世界模型在专家动作上表现尚可，但对多样化非专家轨迹会忽略动作或生成视觉无效 rollout；具体模型规模、数据量、baseline 和提升幅度未在摘要中给出。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tests whether action-conditioned robotic world models actually follow commanded actions, especially outside expert-demonstration trajectories.
summary_en.importance: It contributes a diagnostic benchmark and alignment method for embodied world models. The relevance to LLM pretraining is indirect, but the failure mode is useful for thinking about conditional generative modeling.
summary_en.technical_approach: WorldEcho evaluates action following through visual integrity and SE(3) trajectory alignment. WorldSync improves action conditioning through broader consequence coverage, grounded action representations, and intervention-effect alignment.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports that current world models execute expert actions reasonably well but often ignore diverse off-expert actions or produce invalid visual rollouts. It does not specify model sizes, datasets, baselines, or exact gains.

recommendation.zh: 只需看 WorldEcho 的诊断设计；它提醒条件生成评测不能只测训练分布附近动作。
recommendation.en: Read the WorldEcho diagnostic setup; it is a useful reminder that conditional generation should not be evaluated only near the training action distribution.

paper.title: There Is No Neutral Harness: Modern LLM Leaderboards Are Manufactured by Config-Fragile Items
paper.abstract: Multiple-choice benchmarks fix the questions and the correct answers, but not the harness: the order of the options, the wording of the prompt, and whether a language model's answer is read from generated text or from per-option likelihoods. Work on this harness sensitivity reports it as aggregate score variance, leaving unexamined which items the variance falls on and whether they are the items that separate one model from the next. We treat the evaluation harness of large language models (LLMs

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决的是 LLM 多选评测中的一个更细粒度问题：benchmark 固定了题目和答案，但没有固定 evaluation harness。选项顺序、prompt 格式、生成式解析还是 likelihood 打分，都会改变单题正确性。已有工作多看总分或排名方差，论文进一步追问：排名差距到底来自稳定题目，还是来自对 harness 很敏感的题目。
summary.importance: 这是一篇评测方法论文，但对预训练研究有直接影响。预训练 recipe、数据配比、checkpoint selection 和 scaling curve 经常依赖 MMLU、ARC 这类多选评测。如果相邻模型的差距主要由 config-fragile items 支撑，那么小幅榜单差异不能直接解释为模型能力差异。贡献量级不在于提出新 benchmark，而在于把 harness sensitivity 从 aggregate score 下钻到 item-level，并给出 pairwise leaderboard gap decomposition。这会影响模型比较、消融判断、数据实验早停和公开 leaderboard 的解读方式。
summary.technical_approach: 论文把 evaluation harness 显式当作自变量，构造 fragility grid。实验覆盖 12 个 open-weight instruction-tuned models，来自 4 个模型家族；题目为 4 个 benchmark 的 3,679 个多选 items；每个 model-item 都在 26 个合理 harness configurations 下评测。三类 harness 轴包括 option order、prompt format 和 scoring method。每个三元组得到一个 correctness bit。基于这个张量，论文定义单模型单题的 robust / config-fragile：如果 26 个配置下正确性不变，则为 robust；如果发生翻转，则为 fragile。随后把任意两个相邻模型的分数差距拆成两部分：双方都稳定回答的题目贡献，以及至少一方会随配置翻转的题目贡献。这个设计的关键点是控制模型权重、题目集合、解码设置，只让 harness 变化，因此能回答“榜单排序由哪些题目支撑”而不是只回答“总分波动多大”。论文还分析了 benchmark compression：用 item discrimination 选择小子集时，是否会保留甚至放大 fragile items。
summary.experiments: 核心结果很尖锐。第一，同一模型的 accuracy 更像一个区间而不是一个点；例如 gemma4-31b 在同一权重和同一题集上，不同配置下从 31% 到 89%。论文报告称，模型被记为正确的答案中，最多 85% 可以被另一个同样合理的配置翻成错误。第二，相邻模型排序几乎不由稳定题目决定。在 11 个相邻模型对中，只看双方都稳定回答的题目，5 对逐题完全相同，4 对只差 1 道题，剩余 2 对虽有差异但正负抵消为 0。完整题集上有非零 gap 的 10 对仍会被排序，而 config-fragile items 平均承载 95.7% 的 pairwise gap；按题目池化后达到 99.7%。第三，选择 harness 等价于在一组可辩护流程中选择赢家。12 个模型中有 4 个能在某个配置下排名第一，8 个能进入前三；mixtral-8x7b 在 reference harness 下排第 11，但在另一个配置下排第 1。两个主要第一名模型分别覆盖 24/26 个配置，median lead 为 181.5 和 98.5 items；另外两个只在单个配置下第一，领先 1 和 3 items。第四，压缩 benchmark 不会自动去除 fragile items。item discrimination 与 config-fragility 的相关系数为 0.28，95% CI 为 0.25 到 0.30；最高 discrimination items 的平均 fragility 为 0.96，高于全 benchmark 的 0.85。压缩到 100 题时，full benchmark 的 champion count 为 4，随机 100 题平均为 5.1，按 discrimination 选 100 题平均为 5.7，seeded tie-break 下范围为 4 到 7。第五，scoring method 是最关键的 harness 轴。固定其他轴时，对 scoring choice 保持 robust 的 mean accuracy 为 0.31，低于 prompt format 的 0.40 和 option order 的 0.60，说明 generation-vs-likelihood 的选择对多选评测结论影响很大。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读 introduction 中的问题拆解和 contribution bullets，它们把 aggregate variance 与 item-level leaderboard identification 的差别讲得很清楚。方法部分重点看 fragility grid 的构造、robust/config-fragile item 定义，以及 pairwise gap decomposition 的公式或实现逻辑。结果部分优先看三个图表：模型 accuracy band、相邻模型 gap 的 robust/fragile 分解、不同 harness 下 rank-one/top-three 分布。benchmark compression 一节也值得细看，因为很多内部评测会用 IRT 或 discrimination 做短榜，论文指出这种压缩可能保留最不稳定的题。实现上建议检查开源 per-item records 和 analysis script，尤其是 generation parsing 与 per-option likelihood scoring 的细节；这些细节往往决定复现实验能否对齐。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a fine-grained failure mode in multiple-choice LLM evaluation. Benchmarks fix questions and gold answers, but they usually do not fix the evaluation harness: option order, prompt formatting, and whether answers are read from generated text or per-option likelihoods. Prior work mostly measured score or rank variance. This paper asks a sharper question: when rankings change, which individual items carry the model gap, and do stable items identify the same ordering?
summary_en.importance: The contribution is an evaluation contribution, but it matters for pretraining research. Pretraining recipes, data-mixture decisions, checkpoint selection, and scaling analyses often rely on MMLU-like multiple-choice scores. If adjacent-model gaps are mostly carried by config-fragile items, small leaderboard differences should not be treated as clean evidence of model capability. The main value is the item-level decomposition of leaderboard gaps into robust and fragile mass, rather than another aggregate sensitivity measurement.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper promotes the evaluation harness to an explicit independent variable. It builds a fragility grid over 26 defensible harness configurations, spanning option order, prompt format, and scoring method. The experiment evaluates 12 open-weight instruction-tuned models from 4 families on 3,679 items from 4 benchmarks. For every model-item-configuration triple, it records a binary correctness value. An item is robust for a model if its correctness is invariant across all 26 configurations; it is config-fragile if it flips. With this tensor, each adjacent pairwise leaderboard gap is decomposed into the part supported by items both models answer stably and the part carried by fragile items. The design keeps weights, items, and decoding fixed so that harness choice is the moving factor. The paper also studies benchmark compression, asking whether item-discrimination-based subsets filter out or preserve fragile items.
summary_en.experiments: The reported effects are large. A model’s accuracy becomes a band rather than a point: gemma4-31b ranges from 31% to 89% on the same weights and the same items under different configurations. Across the roster, up to 85% of credited answers can be flipped to wrong by another defensible configuration. Adjacent-model rankings are not identified by stable items. Among 11 adjacent pairs, on items both models answer stably, 5 pairs are identical item by item, 4 differ on exactly one item, and the remaining 2 have disagreements that cancel to zero. Yet the full benchmark still orders every one of the 10 pairs with a nonzero full-set gap. Config-fragile items carry 95.7% of a pair’s gap on average, rising to 99.7% when pooling items rather than averaging pairs. Harness choice also changes winners: 4 of 12 models reach rank one under some configuration, and 8 of 12 reach the top three. mixtral-8x7b is 11th under the reference harness and 1st under another. The two models that win 24 of 26 configurations have median leads of 181.5 and 98.5 items out of 3,679; the other two single-configuration winners lead by only 1 and 3 items. Benchmark compression does not solve the issue. Item discrimination correlates with config-fragility at 0.28 with a 95% CI of 0.25 to 0.30, and the most discriminative items have mean fragility 0.96 versus 0.85 over the full benchmark. When compressed to 100 items, the champion count rises from 4 on the full benchmark to 5.1 for random subsets and 5.7 for discrimination-selected subsets, with a seeded tie-break range from 4 to 7. The scoring axis is especially important: holding other axes fixed, mean accuracy robust to scoring choice is 0.31, compared with 0.40 for prompt format and 0.60 for option order.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read the introduction and contribution bullets carefully; they frame the difference between aggregate score noise and item-level identification of leaderboard orderings. In the methods, focus on the fragility grid, the robust/config-fragile definition, and the pairwise gap decomposition. In the results, prioritize the figures or tables showing accuracy bands, adjacent-pair robust-versus-fragile gap mass, and rank-one/top-three changes across harnesses. The benchmark compression analysis is also important for teams using short internal evals or IRT-style item selection. For replication or internal adoption, inspect the released per-item records and scripts, especially the generation-parsing and per-option-likelihood scoring implementations.

recommendation.zh: 这篇会直接改变你看 benchmark ablation 的方式：先看脆弱题分布再谈 recipe 优劣，建议立刻把 item-level harness sweep 加进内部评测。
recommendation.en: This should change how you read benchmark ablations: inspect item-level fragility before claiming recipe gains, and add harness sweeps to your internal eval stack.

paper.title: Most of the LLM routing gap is task type
paper.abstract: An LLM router picks which model should answer each query. The appeal is that models fail on different questions. Whatever single model is best overall still gets some wrong, and another model in the pool gets many of those right. Getting that choice right every time is the ceiling, and a router is an attempt to approach it. However, recent work reports that routers do not get close. Across 21 routing methods on five benchmarks, sharply different designs land within a fraction of a point of each

summary.core_problem: 为什么现有的 LLM 路由（Routing）方法性能普遍不佳，难以接近理论上限？
summary.importance: 通过大规模实证分析指出，当前 LLM 路由的性能瓶颈主要在于任务类型（Task Type），而非模型间的细微差异，挑战了现有路由方法设计的核心假设。
summary.technical_approach: 在 5 个基准测试上评估了 21 种路由方法，发现它们性能差异极小且远低于上限。为了探究原因，让 14 个模型回答 294 个问题（涵盖 3 种语言、7 种任务类型）。通过重复运行矩阵并分析模型-问题对的得分差异，揭示了任务类型对路由效果的决定性影响。
summary.experiments: 14 个模型，294 个问题，3 种语言，7 种任务类型。发现 5.37% 的模型-问题对在两次相同运行中得分不同，表明运行间的波动是常态，而任务类型是导致路由差距的主要因素。

summary_en.core_problem: Why do existing LLM routing methods generally perform poorly and struggle to approach the theoretical ceiling?
summary_en.importance: Through large-scale empirical analysis, it points out that the performance bottleneck of current LLM routing lies mainly in the task type rather than subtle differences between models, challenging the core assumptions of existing routing method designs.
summary_en.technical_approach: Evaluated 21 routing methods across 5 benchmarks, finding minimal performance differences and a huge gap from the ceiling. To investigate, 14 models were tasked with answering 294 questions (across 3 languages and 7 task types). By rerunning the matrix and analyzing score differences for model-question pairs, it revealed the decisive impact of task type on routing effectiveness.
summary_en.experiments: 14 models, 294 questions, 3 languages, 7 task types. Found that 5.37% of model-question pairs scored differently in two identical runs, indicating that run-to-run variance is normal, and task type is the primary factor causing the routing gap.

recommendation.zh: 揭示了 LLM Routing 现阶段的本质困境：不同 router 性能差不多，且打不过直接 call 最强模型，核心原因是 task type 的 variance 盖过了 router 的区分度。做 MoE 路由或 model ensemble 的必看。
recommendation.en: Reveals the fundamental dilemma of current LLM routing: different routers perform similarly and fail to beat simply calling the strongest model, primarily because task type variance overshadows router discriminability. A must-read for those working on MoE routing or model ensembling.

paper.title: LitReview Arena: Evaluating Literature Review Agents with Battle-Style Peer Review Platform
paper.abstract: Literature reviews are essential to scientific progress, but rigorously evaluating automatically generated reviews remains difficult because many aspects of research utility depend on expert judgment rather than reference-overlap metrics. We introduce LitReview Arena, a battle-style evaluation platform with a structured protocol tailored to literature review quality: domain experts with AI paper-writing experience compare anonymized drafts, are matched to topics within their expertise, and provi

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作解决的是一个评测问题：自动生成 literature review 到底该怎么评，尤其是那些无法靠 reference overlap、citation accuracy 或 coverage heuristic 直接判定的部分。作者认为，文献综述真正影响研究者使用价值的地方，恰恰是最难自动打分的部分，比如结构是否合理、论证是否站得住、研究空白是否有判断力、未来方向是否具体而不空泛。现有 benchmark 往往能评检索、评引用、评表面覆盖，但很难评“这篇综述是否真的像一个懂行的人写的”。因此他们提出 LitReview Arena，用 battle-style 的专家偏好评测协议，把 literature review 评测做成接近同行评审的流程。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究本身不是直接方法贡献，但对 post-train、agent、deep research、LLM-as-judge 和高质量科研写作系统的评测很有参考价值。它的重要性主要有三层。第一，它说明在开放式科研任务里，静态 rubric 和自动指标很容易失真，尤其在结构组织和研究建议这类高层判断上。第二，它给出了一套更可信的人工评测协议：专家筛选、主题-专长匹配、匿名对战、分维度投票。第三，它不仅收集了约 3k 专家判断，还用这些偏好信号去校准低成本 evaluator，把离线自动评测和专家偏好对齐起来。对做训练信号设计的人，这一点尤其有用，因为它意味着专家偏好可以不只用于 leaderboard，也可以反过来做 reward model 或 evaluator calibration。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是把 literature review 评测从“单篇绝对打分”改成“匿名双边对战 + 结构化维度判断”。平台设计有四个关键点。第一，annotator 不是开放众包，而是限定为有 AI 论文写作经验的领域研究者。作者的理由很直接：综述结构、研究空白、方向建议这些维度，离开领域知识很难稳定判断。第二，query 不是随机构造 prompt，而是从真实、高被引 survey 中抽取主题，保证任务本身有学术意义，也让评审者更容易形成稳定标准。第三，做 expertise matching，把题目分配给对应领域的专家，尽量模拟真实 peer review。第四，评测维度不是单一 overall preference，而是五个专门面向 literature review 的维度：D1 文献覆盖，D2 论断支撑，D3 文章结构，D4 研究建议质量，D5 整体效用。

这套设计和一般 arena 的区别在于，它不是只追求可扩展的人类偏好采集，而是试图把“科研写作中的主观判断”制度化。全文还做了第二层工作：基于 LitReviewBench 的专家偏好数据，训练或校准一个低成本 evaluator，用于离线评测。作者明确指出，未经校准的 LLM-as-a-judge 与专家偏好存在明显偏差，甚至会给出错误的系统排序；因此他们不是直接拿 judge 当替代品，而是先用专家数据做对齐。这个思路比直接报告一个 judge accuracy 更扎实，因为它承认了 judge 本身也是需要监督的。
summary.experiments:
关键结果有四个。第一，作者收集了约 3k 条专家 judgment，每条都包含五个维度的胜负结果，而不是只有 overall vote。第二，在与人类撰写综述的 decisive matches 中，当前最强系统在 D5 overall utility 上的胜率只有 23.0%，说明距离人类水平还有明显差距。第三，差距最大的维度是 D3 paper structure 和 D4 research suggestions，作者用大约 200 rating points 的落后幅度来描述这一差距。这说明模型不是简单“不会找论文”，而是更难形成有判断力的组织框架和非模板化研究建议。第四，agentic systems 明显优于纯 language models，但代价是平均约 15× 的 token 开销，说明检索、规划、多轮写作确实带来质量提升，但 test-time compute 成本不低。

另一个很实用的结果是 evaluator 校准。未经校准的 LLM judge 与专家排序相关性较低，在 D5 上只有 ρ≈0.467；用 LitReviewBench 做校准后，相关性提升到 ρ≈0.792。这个数字说明专家偏好数据确实能显著改善离线评测器的可用性。对做 reward modeling 或 evaluator design 的人，这比单纯说“judge 还不错”更有信息量。
summary.reading_guide:
这篇适合泛读，不需要逐节精抠。先看 Introduction，把作者为什么认为 literature review 不能只靠自动指标评清楚。然后重点看 protocol design：annotator 选择、topic 来源、expertise matching、五个维度定义。这部分决定了数据是否可信。接着看主要结果图表，尤其是 human vs model 的胜率、各维度差距、agentic vs pure LM 的 token 成本对比，以及 evaluator calibration 前后的相关性变化。

如果时间有限，20–30 分钟足够抓住主线。建议优先看任务定义、评测协议、主结果表、judge calibration。可以跳过较细的实现描述。阅读时要注意一个边界：它评的是 literature review agent，不是通用 LLM pretrain 方法，所以更适合作为“如何构造高质量开放式科研任务评测”的参考，而不是直接指导预训练 recipe。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper tackles an evaluation problem: how should we assess automatically generated literature reviews, especially the parts that cannot be captured by reference overlap, citation correctness, or simple coverage heuristics. The authors argue that the most important aspects of a useful review—field structure, support for claims, quality of research gaps, and usefulness of future directions—are exactly the parts that resist automatic scoring. Existing benchmarks can evaluate retrieval and surface-level grounding, but they struggle to answer whether a review actually reads like something a knowledgeable researcher would trust. LitReview Arena is proposed as a battle-style, expert-preference evaluation protocol designed to approximate peer review for literature-review agents.
summary_en.importance: This is not a direct contribution to pretraining methods, but it is relevant to post-training, research agents, evaluator design, and expert-aligned supervision. Its importance comes from three places. First, it shows that static rubrics and automatic metrics are badly limited for open-ended scientific writing, especially on high-level dimensions such as structure and research suggestions. Second, it offers a more credible human-evaluation protocol: expert-only annotators, topic–expertise matching, blind pairwise comparison, and dimension-wise judgments. Third, it does not stop at collecting preference data. It uses roughly 3k expert judgments to calibrate a low-cost offline evaluator, which is useful for anyone thinking about reward models, evaluator alignment, or scalable supervision for research-oriented agents.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The core idea is to replace absolute scoring of a single review with anonymized pairwise battles plus structured dimension-wise judgments. The platform has four main design choices. First, annotators are not crowd workers; they are domain experts with AI paper-writing experience. The motivation is straightforward: judging review structure, field organization, and research directions requires field-level judgment. Second, the prompts are not synthetic topics. They are derived from real, highly cited surveys so that the tasks correspond to recognizable and academically meaningful review problems. Third, the platform performs expertise matching, assigning topics to reviewers within their area, which makes the setup closer to actual peer review. Fourth, the evaluation is decomposed into five literature-review-specific dimensions: D1 literature coverage, D2 claim support, D3 paper structure, D4 research suggestions quality, and D5 overall utility.

What distinguishes this from generic arena evaluation is that the battle format is not just a scaling trick for preference collection. It is used to operationalize subjective scientific judgment in a more disciplined way. The paper also adds a second layer: using LitReviewBench as calibration data for a low-cost evaluator. The authors show that off-the-shelf LLM-as-a-judge is substantially misaligned with expert preferences and can produce incorrect system rankings. Instead of treating the judge as a drop-in replacement for experts, they explicitly supervise or calibrate it with expert preference data. That is a more careful and more useful framing for evaluator design.
summary_en.experiments:
There are four headline results. First, the benchmark contains about 3k expert judgments, each with outcomes on all five dimensions rather than only an overall preference. Second, in decisive matches against human-written drafts, even the strongest current systems achieve only a 23.0% win rate on D5 overall utility, which indicates a large remaining gap to human performance. Third, the largest deficits appear on D3 paper structure and D4 research suggestions, with models trailing humans by roughly 200 rating points. This is an important diagnosis: the bottleneck is not just retrieval or citation accuracy, but coherent field organization and non-generic research insight.
